title: Inverse variation models
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest point, reciprocal functions, covers the asymptotes and quadrants of the graph of y = k/x, not modelling inverse variation in context such as speed and travel time, so this new point should be added as its own point.

draft.title: Inverse variation models
card: In an inverse variation, y = k/x, where k is a fixed number called the constant. As x gets bigger, y gets smaller.
Doubling x halves y. Tripling x divides y by 3. The product x × y always equals k.
The graph is a curve called a hyperbola. It never touches either axis.
Example: a 120 km trip takes t = 120/s hours at a speed of s km/h. At 60 km/h, t = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours. At 120 km/h, t = 1 hour. Doubling the speed halved the time.
draft.remember: In y = k/x, x × y stays the same, so when one doubles the other halves.

a.q: y varies inversely with x. When x = 4, y = 12. What is y when x = 8?
a.why: Here k = x × y = 4 × 12 = 48, so y = 48/8 = 6. Doubling x halves y. The answer 24 comes from doubling y, which treats the relationship as direct rather than inverse.
a.clue: Find k first by multiplying x and y.

b.q: Leila's trip is 240 km. At an average speed of 80 km/h it takes 3 hours. If she slows to an average of 60 km/h, how long does the trip take?
b.why: Time = 240/speed, so t = 240 ÷ 60 = 4 hours. Check: 80 × 3 = 240 and 60 × 4 = 240, so the product stays the same. Slower speed means more time, so 2.25 hours is wrong. That answer comes from multiplying 3 by 60/80, which treats the relationship as direct.
b.clue: Distance stays 240 km, so speed × time stays the same.
